description: Use this when the user wants their own know-how captured (interview me about how I approve refunds, write the SOP for our month-end close, I'm handing over my job) or wants someone else interviewed (send Sarah an Extraction about how she prices renewals). For the user: participantMode self. For someone else: participantMode email with that person's email; the topic says what they should talk through, and RuleFoundry emails them. Before this tool, call rulefoundry_prepare_extraction_request as soon as the user asks, before you ask them anything: it is read-only and returns the one question to ask, which is your confirmation, so never ask your own first. Call this tool only after the user said yes to that question, with the same values and the idempotencyKey it returned; without that key this tool only returns the preview again and creates nothing. Reuse a key only to retry that exact confirmed request as the same actor; replay does not resend email. Creation needs extractions:write and does not consume Extraction quota. Where Projects are on, a new Extraction goes into a Project, and its finished rules into that Project's knowledge base. Ask the preview's question as your one question: it covers the go-ahead and which Project; pass projectId only for an existing Project the user chose. The interview is by voice: where the host shows RuleFoundry's panel it opens there, and appUrl opens it on the RuleFoundry page. Share that link and say the interviewer asks the questions and writes the rules as they talk. Never describe the interview by a duration or time limit unless the user asked for one. Failed or unknown emailDelivery still returns an existing request. When emailProblem is set, tell the user its message and ask whether to send to a different address or try again (rulefoundry_update_extraction_request_email); never pick an address yourself and never retry without their yes. appUrl is for the user only: it never lets the participant in, so never suggest sharing it with them; only RuleFoundry's email invitation does. Do not use this to pull data out of documents or forms.

confirmCreateAndSend.description: Always true. The user's yes is given to the preview the first call returns.

description.description: Optional Extraction description confirmed by the user.

expectedMinutes.description: Only when the user asks for a specific length: the call length in minutes. Omit it otherwise; the interviewer paces itself and ends when the expert has nothing left. Never mention or ask about call length or a time limit unless the user raised it.

idempotencyKey.description: On the first call, any fresh opaque key. After the user says yes to the preview, the idempotencyKey that preview returned. Reuse it only to retry the same request.

participantEmail.description: Exact confirmed participant email; required only when participantMode is email.

participantMode.description: Use self for the signed-in user or email for another participant.

projectId.description: Only when the user chose one of the Projects the preview listed: its id. Omit it to start a new Project named after the topic.

topic.description: Exact Extraction topic confirmed by the user.

name: rulefoundry_create_extraction_request

emailDelivery.description: The invitation email: not_applicable for a self Extraction; sent when our email service accepted it; delivered or bounced when the recipient's mail server reported so; failed when it could not be sent; unknown with no recorded outcome. The request exists in every case.

canRetry.description: True when sending to the same address again usually works.

message.description: Plain words for the user, naming the address. Tell them this.

emailProblem.description: Why the invitation email did not arrive, or null. When set, tell the user the message and ask whether to send to a different address or try again; never pick an address yourself and never retry without their yes (rulefoundry_update_extraction_request_email).

idempotencyKey.description: Pass this back, with the same values, only after the user says yes.

projects.description: Projects the user may add this Extraction to, newest first; absent when Projects are off.

question.description: Ask the user exactly this, as one question.

title: Create an Extraction request
